newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French 10-year bond yields fell to their lowest level since February 24, 1994 as debt markets took comfort from the decision by the U.S. Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged.
The yield on the 6.50 percent 2006 OAT fell to 6.13 percent from 6.19 percent on Tuesday, while the spread over 10-year Bunds remained steady at three basis points.

While some analysts said the Fed's inaction may have been politically motivated, others said the positive response in bond markets stemmed from the perception that inflationary pressures may not be strong enough yet to prompt a rate rise.

"It's not that they're not worried about inflation, but more that they don't see enough evidence of inflationary pressures to take the necessary action," said Andrew Davies, bond strategist at London Bond Broking.

The positive reaction to the U.S. decision allowed the December bond future to open at a new contract high, leaving a gap between 124.14 and 124.26, and it then broke through a series of resistance levels during the day to hit 124.64.
Traders also said benign German and French inflation figures released today reinforced the view that inflation was not a problem in Europe.
CADES said it would only be selling 12 billion francs of bonds this week, less than the 18 billion many had expected. It will be selling a new 2005 bond.
Lead managers Banque Nationale de Paris and Credit Agricole said the issue would be on Thursday and the bond would be priced between five and seven basis points over government bonds.
The franc was relatively stable during Wednesday. It was trading at 3.3834 late in the session, up from a low of 3.3872 earlier in the day.
